title: PeopleHub — Sparse Fieldsets
objective: Salary and performance data are visible to HR only. As an ordinary employee, get them anyway — without touching anyone's session.

verifier.condition: A response to a non-HR user contains the salary or performanceRating property of an employee.

weakness: Property-level filtering is applied to the default response shape, but the sparse-fieldset 'fields' parameter projects straight from the raw record and bypasses it.
seededData: Users alice (employee) and hana (HR); five synthetic employees with salary and performance rating. In-memory.

credentials.label: Employee
credentials.note: The default responses show no pay information.

hints: Read the API reference carefully — which query parameters does the directory accept?
A filter that decides what to remove is only as good as the code path that uses it.
burpNotes: Compare the default JSON for a single employee with what the documented query parameters return. Property names to try come from the full record shape.
